title: Acid drops
subtitle: Hard, sharp boiled sweets made with sugar syrup and citric acid
excerpt: Acid drops are hard-boiled sweets with a sharp, clean sourness from citric acid added to the sugar after cooking. The syrup is cooked to hard-crack stage, poured onto an oiled slab, worked briefly as it cools, then pulled into a rope and cut into pieces. The technique requires working fast once the sugar leaves the pan.
sourceNotes: Acid drops are one of the oldest British boiled sweets, documented since the early nineteenth century. They are made with lemon flavouring and citric acid, which gives the characteristic sharp flavour distinct from simple sweetness. The technique is standard pulled-sugar confectionery, documented in confectionery reference texts including those of the Confectioners' Union.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Store in an airtight tin between layers of baking paper. Keep at room temperature for up to 3 weeks. Do not refrigerate; moisture causes the sweets to become sticky.

glossaryTerms.definition: A confectionery technique in which cooked sugar at or just below hard-crack stage is folded and stretched repeatedly while still warm and pliable. Pulling incorporates air into the mass, which creates a satin, slightly opaque finish rather than a clear glass-like one. Acid drops use a brief pull rather than an extended one; the goal is even texture and workable temperature, not high aeration.

content.text: Acid drops use a brief version of

: the cooked sugar is worked on an oiled surface just long enough to incorporate the citric acid and reach a workable rolling temperature, then formed into a rope and cut. Have everything in place before the sugar leaves the pan.

Sugar syrup at hard-crack stage is approximately 150 degrees Celsius. It sets fast and sticks to skin. Keep children away, have cold water accessible, and wear heatproof gloves when working the sugar on the slab.
Lightly oil a marble slab or large baking tray. Have a pair of oiled scissors or a lightly oiled knife ready for cutting.

Put the sugar, glucose syrup, water, and cream of tartar in a medium saucepan. Stir over low heat until the sugar dissolves. Increase to medium-high heat and cook without stirring to 150 degrees Celsius. Remove from heat. Add the food colouring if using and swirl the pan to mix.
Pour onto the oiled slab. Sprinkle the citric acid over the surface. Leave for 60 to 90 seconds until the edges cool enough to touch with gloved hands.

Using oiled gloves, fold the edges into the centre and begin working the mass, folding and stretching. As it cools it will become firmer and more pliable. Work for 3 to 4 minutes until it is still warm but stiff enough to roll.

Roll into a long rope about 1 cm diameter. Snip or cut into 2 cm pieces. Leave on baking paper to harden completely, about 20 to 30 minutes. Dust with a little icing sugar to prevent sticking before storing.
